questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange at Boston University allowed me to take courses in different fields such as sociology, literature, genders and sexualities and critical race theory. Taking these courses broadened by academic horizons and made me more aware of power structures and relations that dominate not only academia, but also the wider world. I feel this exchange has given me more empathy and understanding for other people, cultures and a will to change the world for the better through my academic pursuits.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, I did not have any major difficulties starting the semester at BU

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: It mostly consisted of helpful emails from BU's study abroad coordinator, as well as emails about events etc. for study abroad students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was not much of an orientation, but this was due to Covid-19

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, I checked out Facebook groups and found a co-op

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive! But will give you a better understanding of local life than living in a dormitory (which can be more expensive even)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy, I can't remember any big issues

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't remember much to be honest. I had to go to a separate building to get my student ID, which was trickiest.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Visiting the administration office, emailing

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful! I had some issues understanding the levels system of classes. I.e. which ones were undergrad level vs graduate level. Professors were helpful in this regard however.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Figure out the level system first, and apply to your courses of choice well ahead of the deadline

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very insightful, respectful and interested professors, who were very caring about the students and passionate about their fields

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was adequate and comparable to the level at my home university of Copenhagen University

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more conversational and interactive, and the professors started every class with a pronouns round (e.g. 'my name is X and my pronouns are she/her') which made it much more comfortable to be an LGBT student than at my home university, which can feel alienating as an LGBT student.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Video Reporting
Critical Studies: Black Diaspora and Practice
Seminar: Genders, Sexualities and Youth Cultures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of these. They were insightful and unlike courses I could have taken at my home university. The teachers were from diverse backgrounds and had a personal relationship to the topic matters.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were interesting student-led clubs but their meet times were always when I had class, so I never got to attend any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs centred around specific interests (beekeeping, sports, etc)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going online/on apps and finding the local nightlife, music and events scene

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to basement concerts

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find people/other internationals online/ on apps (Bumble BFF, Lex, Discords, etc)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Roommate etiquette, sharing of groceries

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and honesty of Americans, and their social awareness and responsibility

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Study at a good cafe instead of the BU libraries (the lighting is awful), be spontaneous and go to events/things you might not have considered at home, do the reading and engage with your course mates, try to create relationships with your professors

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a good time

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all kinds of people, learning lots from the courses which have really broadened my perspective

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Administrative tasks involving health care and immigration

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it! It's tons of fun.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
